title: Volume 0 · Making the System Usable
subtitle: Lessons 6–10: units of measure, warehouses, users and roles, permissions, naming series and the settings that bite later
outcomes: Configure units of measure and conversions that survive real purchasing
Create a warehouse tree with correct stock and adjustment accounts
Create users with roles that match what each person actually does
Restrict rows and actions with user permissions and role permissions
Set the stock and selling settings that decide valuation, credit control and document numbering

slides.title: Units that multiply without breaking valuation
bullets: UOMs are master data: a typo here becomes a wrong stock balance that looks plausible
Create only the units the client buys and sells in, then convert between them explicitly
No unit is more real than another: one Box equals twelve Nos is a conversion factor, not a separate product
Tick 'Must be whole number' for physical units so nobody invoices 0.4 of a blender
Weight-based units need decimals, so decide per unit instead of applying one rule everywhere

rows: Conversion appears in the UOM list for Box

slides.notes: The classic consultant failure is discovering, three months in, that stock was received in boxes at the piece rate. Build conversions before any stock movement, and test one conversion on a draft Purchase Receipt. If the client buys in boxes of twelve and sells single pieces, both units are legitimate and the conversion factor is the contract between them.

slides.title: One box, twelve pieces, one valuation
bullets: A test Purchase Receipt of 1 Box posts a stock balance of 12 Nos, not 1
The stock ledger shows quantity in the stock UOM, with the box quantity preserved on the document
Entering 0.5 against a whole-number unit is refused at save
Valuation stays per Nos, so the rate you type per box is divided correctly
Stock reports agree with the warehouse total when converted back to boxes
slides.notes: Ask the learner to predict the stock balance before saving, then check it. This is the same prediction habit used for tax totals, and it is the core skill of a functional consultant. Watch for the trap where the client's purchase UOM is a box but the item's stock UOM is Nos: the conversion must exist before the first receipt, or the balance will be wrong and reposting is required.

callout.title: Conversions after go-live
callout.text: Adding a conversion factor later does not rewrite history. If stock already moved in the wrong unit, you need a stock reconciliation, not a settings change.

slides.title: A warehouse tree with accounts behind it
bullets: Warehouses are physical locations and each one must point at a stock account for valuation postings
Separate warehouses for main stock, retail counter, assembly and returns make movement visible
A returns warehouse is not bureaucracy: it is how you separate resellable stock from quarantined stock
Warehouse names carry the abbreviation, so reports read 'Main Warehouse - SM' consistently
Set the default warehouse once at company level, then override per document when reality demands it

rows: Name ends with the company suffix
Each warehouse is selectable on stock documents

slides.notes: Four warehouses is the smallest tree that teaches the concepts and still fits a real distributor: buy into main, move to retail, consume components on the assembly floor, quarantine returns. Explain that stock never 'teleports': a transfer is a document, and the trial balance stays the same during a transfer because both sides use the same stock account unless you deliberately use different accounts per warehouse.

slides.title: Balances per warehouse that reconcile to the total
bullets: Stock Balance report lists all four warehouses with zero quantity before any transaction
A transfer of 5 units from Main to Retail leaves the company total unchanged at 5
The stock ledger shows two rows: −5 in Main and +5 in Retail on the same timestamp
Warehouse-wise profit and loss shows stock value per location when accounts differ
The default warehouse on a new Stock Entry is Main Warehouse - SM
slides.notes: The transfer test proves two ideas at once: that stock is tracked per location and that a transfer is not a purchase or a sale. If the learner sees a value change during a transfer, the warehouses are pointing at different stock accounts, which is a deliberate design for some businesses but must be explained, not accidental.

callout.title: Name warehouses by place, not by person
callout.text: 'Ali's Store' becomes a problem when Ali leaves. Use the physical location and keep people in the warehouse contact fields.

slides.title: Give each person the smallest menu that works
bullets: A user is a login; a role is a bundle of DocType permissions; a role profile is a reusable bundle of roles
Create named users, never shared logins, because the audit trail is worthless otherwise
Accounts User can create invoices but not cancel them; Accounts Manager can do both
Stock User fits a storekeeper; Sales User fits a showroom assistant; System Manager is for the consultant only
Set the timezone per user so document timestamps read correctly in reports

rows: Finance Team = Accounts User + Accounts Manager

slides.notes: Demonstrate the login rather than describing it. Sign out as administrator, sign in as the storekeeper, and let the learner see a shorter menu. That single experience prevents most of the 'everyone is an administrator' outcomes that make implementations hard to audit. Role profiles save time later when the client hires a fifth accounts person.

slides.title: Menus that match job descriptions
bullets: The storekeeper can see Stock and Buying but has no Accounts menu
The accounts manager can create and cancel invoices; the accounts user cannot cancel
The consultant sees everything, which is why you never demo as the consultant
Each user profile shows the correct role list and timezone
Switching users is a one-click test, so run it before every training session
slides.notes: The cancel test is the one that matters commercially: an accounts user who can cancel submitted invoices can silently corrupt the sales ledger. Explain the difference between a role and a role profile, then show how a permission shows up as a greyed-out button rather than an error, which is friendlier for training.

callout.title: Never train as Administrator
callout.text: Administrator bypasses every permission. Demo and train with a real user account, otherwise you will promise buttons that staff cannot see.

slides.title: Row-level restrictions and document numbers
bullets: Role permissions control what a role may do to a DocType: read, write, submit, cancel, delete
User permissions restrict which rows a user sees, for example only their own warehouse
Permlevel fields are hidden from lower levels, which is how credit limits stay with finance
Naming series decide what the client's customers see as an invoice number, so agree the format first
A meaningful series such as SI-2026-00001 is easier to quote on the phone than a random hash

rows: Sales User → Sales Invoice → Read, Write, Create
User farid@, Allow Warehouse: Main Warehouse

slides.notes: Two different ideas are often confused here: role permissions decide verbs, user permissions decide rows. The warehouse restriction is the most valuable example for a distributor, because it stops a storekeeper from posting into another outlet's stock. Naming series is where consultants earn goodwill, because invoice numbers are visible to customers and cannot be changed retroactively.

slides.title: Restricted users see less, not errors
bullets: The storekeeper's stock report lists one warehouse and the totals are that warehouse only
The storekeeper can create a Stock Entry but cannot cancel a submitted Sales Invoice
New invoices follow the agreed series and never skip a number within a period
The sales user sees the invoice form but not the credit limit field at permlevel 1
Administrator still sees everything, which is the control case for every permission test
slides.notes: Always run the permission test twice: once as the restricted user and once as Administrator. If both look the same, no permission was applied. This habit catches the most common implementation defect, which is a system that appears secure in the demo because the demo was done with the wrong account.

callout.title: Numbering is a contract
callout.text: Agree the series with the client's auditor before the first real invoice. Renumbering afterwards means cancelled documents and an uncomfortable conversation.

slides.title: The stock and selling settings that decide behaviour
bullets: Valuation method is chosen once per company: FIFO or moving average, and changed later only through reposting
Allow Negative Stock off is the single most valuable setting for stock accuracy
Check Credit Limit on turns customer limits into a submit-time control instead of a report
Default price list and default warehouse remove two fields from every clerk's daily typing
Enable the settings deliberately and record why, because a future consultant will otherwise guess

rows: Item codes typed by the client are kept
Settings persist and apply to new documents

slides.notes: Explain the consequence of each switch, not the label. Negative stock allowed means valuation can go negative and margins become fictional; credit limit off means the sales team finds out about a bad payer at month end. Item naming by Item Code is a small choice with big consequences: if the client later wants a different code, renaming an item is a database job.

slides.title: Ten checks before you let anyone transact
bullets: Company, abbreviation, currency and fiscal year confirmed against the client's registration documents
Chart of accounts reviewed with finance, with tax accounts typed correctly
Cost centres built and the P&L columns reconcile to the company total
Units and conversions tested with a draft receipt of one box
Warehouses created with the default set and a transfer tested
Users created with role profiles, restricted users verified by logging in as them
Naming series agreed with the auditor, then tested on a draft document
Stock settings recorded: valuation method, negative stock, default warehouse
Selling settings recorded: credit limit, default price list, defaults
Every choice captured on the configuration worksheet with a date and a name

rows: Screenshot of tree and company tab

slides.notes: This slide is the deliverable of Volume 0 and the reason it exists: a signed sheet that says the foundation was built deliberately. Consultants who skip it spend month one arguing about who chose what. Keep the evidence in the client's own drive, not yours, so it survives your engagement.

callout.title: Handover is a meeting
callout.text: Walk the client through the ten checks and collect signatures. A document nobody read is not evidence; a meeting is.

lab.title: Lab · Finish Volume 0 and sign the handover sheet
steps: Create the Box, Set and Kilogram units, then the 1 Box = 12 Nos conversion
Create Main Warehouse, Retail Counter, Assembly Floor and Returns Quarantine
Test a draft Purchase Receipt for 1 Box and confirm the stock balance reads 12 Nos
Create three users with the roles from the lesson, setting timezone Asia/Kuala_Lumpur
Create a Finance Team role profile containing Accounts User and Accounts Manager
Add a user permission restricting farid@ to Main Warehouse and prove it in the stock report
Set Sales Invoice and Purchase Order naming series, then confirm the next invoice number
Set valuation FIFO, negative stock off, credit limit check on and the default price list
Complete the ten-point handover check and collect a name and date against every row
lab.done: Every one of the ten checks passes with evidence attached, the conversion test posted 12 Nos for one box, and the handover sheet is signed by someone other than you.

quiz.question: A client buys in boxes of twelve and sells single pieces. What must exist before the first receipt?
options: Two separate items, one per unit
A Nos stock unit plus a Box purchase unit with a conversion factor of 12
quiz.why: Stock is valued in the stock UOM. A conversion factor of 12 lets the same item be bought in boxes and sold as pieces without inventing a second product.

quiz.question: What is the difference between a role permission and a user permission?
options: A role permission decides which actions a role may perform; a user permission restricts which rows a user sees
A user permission grants administrator rights
quiz.why: Roles govern verbs such as create, submit and cancel. User permissions filter records, for example limiting a storekeeper to one warehouse.

quiz.question: Why is 'Allow Negative Stock' normally turned off?
options: It lets stock and valuation go negative, which makes margins and stock reports fictional
quiz.why: Negative stock hides a missing receipt and produces meaningless valuation. Keeping it off forces the team to record the real movement first.

quiz.question: A transfer of 5 units from Main to Retail should do what to the company's stock total?
options: Leave it unchanged, with −5 in Main and +5 in Retail
quiz.why: A transfer moves quantity between locations. The total stays the same and the stock ledger shows two offsetting rows.

quiz.question: Why agree the invoice naming series before the first real invoice?
options: The number appears on customer-facing documents and cannot be changed retroactively without cancelled records
It determines the chart of accounts
quiz.why: Invoice numbers are a client and auditor contract. Changing the format later leaves a mixed series and questions about the gap.

narration: Volume zero, second half: making the system usable. Start with units. A unit is master data, and a conversion factor is the contract between buying and selling. If the client buys boxes of twelve and sells pieces, you need both units and the factor of twelve before the first receipt, because stock is valued in the stock unit and history cannot be rewritten afterwards. Test it: one box must post twelve pieces, and half a box must be refused. Next, warehouses. Each location points at a stock account, so main stock, retail counter, assembly floor and returns quarantine are four warehouses with one default. Transfer five units and the company total must not move. Then users. A user is a login, a role is a bundle of permissions, and a role profile is a reusable bundle of roles. Create named users, because shared logins destroy the audit trail, and always demonstrate the restricted login rather than the administrator, who bypasses everything. Permissions have two layers: roles decide verbs such as create, submit and cancel, while user permissions decide rows, for example a storekeeper seeing only the main warehouse. Naming series are a contract with the auditor, so agree the format, then test it on a draft. Finally settings: FIFO valuation, negative stock off, credit limit on, default warehouse and price list. Volume zero ends with a ten point handover sheet signed by the client, because a foundation nobody approved is an argument waiting to happen.
